text: You have a thousand customers, paying you €10 a month.
And the first thing you think is: I need more customers.
That is the instinct.
And it is the expensive one.
Because revenue is not a line. It is a surface.
Price on one side, customers on the other,
and your money is the area between them.
Double the customers, and you double the area.
Double the price, and you double it too.
Exactly the same money. Two completely different companies.
Ten thousand customers means ten thousand people to find,
to convince, to onboard, and to keep.
At €180 to acquire each one,
spent before a single one of them pays you back.
Doubling your price takes one afternoon. It costs nothing at all.
Some of them will leave, and even then, the arithmetic is not close.
One lever is free.
The other one is your whole company.
Most founders pull the expensive one first, because it looks like work.
Hiring looks like work. Advertising looks like work.
Changing a number on a pricing page does not.
Colombes puts both levers on the same plate.
You drag one dove, and you watch the surface change.
Then you decide which one you are actually pulling.
Free. No sign-up.
